title: Session stitching proposal and visual runway
body:
Context and goal:

This is a working proposal for how we should (a) stitch distributed request context across the inference stack (API frontend -> router -> model-host -> cache layers -> fallback tiers) and (b) surface that stitched session in a compact, actionable dashboard "visual runway" for rapid incident triage. Aim is to reduce mean time to root cause for model-serving degradations caused by multi-hop routing, cold-KV-cache, or fallback chains.

Why this differs from existing tracing docs:
- Existing guides are good at span design and sampling heuristics; they stop short of a recommended, operator-friendly session reconstruction view that correlates multi-tenant, multi-model fanout.
- This doc prioritizes heuristics to reconstruct a single request journey (session) across services and visualize the critical path, key token-level timings, and quality signals (e.g., rerank fallback, cached prefix hits).

High-level hypothesis to validate:
1) If we provide a synthesized session object with 3–5 anchor points exposed in the UI, oncall engineers will reach a confident hypothesis about cause in 50% less time for common latency incidents.
2) Lightweight session-authored indexing (one additional header per request + minimal KV) gives us >90% stitch rate for requests that hit dedicated or hosted models.

Session model (proposal):
- session_id: UUID at API ingress, propagated with request header Redwood-Session-ID.
- hop_index: incremental integer per service hop (helps ordering when clocks drift).
- anchors (fields we recommend instrumenting at each hop):
  - ingress_ts: timestamp at public API gateway
  - route_decision: model_variant_id + routing_policy (e.g., cost-first / latency-first / canary)
  - kv_cache_status: prefix_hit | partial_hit | miss
  - model_start_ts and model_end_ts: coarse token generation window (ms)
  - fallback_trigger: boolean + reason (e.g., OOM/timeout/no-capacity)
  - tenancy_tag: customer_id or tenant_hash (for multi-tenant drilldown)

Instrumentation checklist (practical):
- Add Redwood-Session-ID at the ingress (prefer using UUIDv7 for sortability).
- Increment hop_index before each outbound call; include basic anchor fields in the HTTP call as headers.
- Model host: emit a condensed span with model_variant, batch_size, kv_cache_status, seq_len, model_start_ts/model_end_ts, gpu_id. Use sampling for full token traces; always emit the condensed anchor.
- Router: log route_decision and capacity_tier chosen; expose fallback_trigger in anchors.
- Cache layer: record prefix_key, hit_ttl, retrieval_latency_ms.

Trace and sampling strategy (practical heuristics):
- Always keep condensed session anchors for 100% of requests at low cardinality (strings + numbers). These are small and high-value for triage.
- Adaptive token-level traces: sample 1% globally, bump to 5–10% for traffic flagged by SLO breaches, and 100% sample for requests that triggered fallback.
- For tenant-sensitive requests (PHI/compliance), redaction rules apply—still record hop timings but avoid text payloads.

Dashboard visual runway (operator view):
Desired single-screen view for a selected session_id with quick actions and drilldowns. Key panels (left-to-right):
1) Summary strip: session_id, tenant, route_decision, final_status (OK/timeout/partial), total_latency_ms, token_count, model_variant.
2) Critical path timeline: compact waterfall showing ingress -> router -> cache -> model(s) -> fallback. Each hop shows latency, batch_size, and a small badge for kv_cache_status or fallback.
3) Heatmap strip for token-level amplification: only when token traces are sampled, show percentiles of token_gen_ms across sequence positions.
4) Quality signals: last N completions scored (e.g., rerank quality, hallucination flag if available), and whether fallback changed the output.
5) Correlated signals: recent alerts, related sessions (same tenant routing to same host), and pod-level CPU/GPU contention at the time.

Design notes / UX heuristics:
- Default to compact mode — one-screen summary with inline expanders for token traces. Operators should not need to leave the view to see the top hypothesis.
- Color semantics: orange for cache misses, red for fallback, blue for normal model decode time.
- Provide a one-click "create investigation" that captures the full session anchors + associated logs and links a Jira ticket template.

Metric definitions to surface in dashboards (these are lightweight, must be integer/float counters or status labels):
- session_stitch_rate: fraction of requests where we could correlate all anchors (goal > 85%).
- session_total_latency_ms: wall-clock from ingress_ts to final_response_ts (p95, p99 panels).
- session_model_decode_ms: sum of model_end_ts - model_start_ts across hops.
- session_kv_prefix_hit_rate: percent with kv_cache_status == prefix_hit.
- fallback_rate_by_reason: grouped counter by fallback_trigger reason.
- stitch_failure_reasons: top categories (missing-header, hop-mismatch, auth-drop).
- correlated_gpu_queue_ms: time spent in device queue across session (needs host-side counters).

Alert candidates (operational):
- session_stitch_rate < 70% sustained for 10m in any region/zone for high-traffic services.
- p99 session_total_latency increases by >30% vs baseline and fallback_rate increases >2x (indicates cascading fallbacks).
- sudden drop in session_kv_prefix_hit_rate accompanied by increase in cache retrieval latency (cache eviction or keyspace shift).

Data retention and cost notes:
- Anchors: keep for 30d at full fidelity (compact, cheap).
- Token traces: keep sampled token-level traces for 7d by default (longer for on-demand investigation slices).
- Indexed session metadata (used for searching) should be sharded by tenant to control cost.

Open questions / risks (engineering discussion points):
- Header propagation at scale: some internal infra currently strips unknown headers at egress — need to audit and add passthrough exceptions.
- Privacy: tenants can include PHI in prompts. Need to ensure we never ingests raw prompt text into long-term trace store unless explicitly allowed.
- Stitch rate for cross-region routing: clock drift and partial logs will reduce stitchability; need to decide if hop_index is authoritative ordering.

Milestones / next steps (recommended):
- Q1 spike (2 weeks): implement Redwood-Session-ID at API ingress + condensed anchor at model host; measure raw stitch_rate. Owner: Liam.
- Q1 prototype (4 weeks): build minimal visual runway UI in console with tabular session search and a timeline panel. Owner: Priya + Product UX.
- Q2 rollout: enable anchors for 100% traffic, token traces sampling adjustments, and add alert rules. Owner: eng-observability.

Notes and quick TODOs (scratch):
- TODO: add header passthrough list to infra PR (INF-1520).
- TODO: define tenant_hash algorithm (avoid storing raw tenant_id in public logs).
- TODO: align on color palette with console team (Sofia).

Appendix: quick instrumentation snippets (pseudo)
- HTTP: header set Redwood-Session-ID: <uuidv7> ; Redwood-Hop-Index: <int> ; Redwood-Anchor: ingress_ts=..., route=model-v2, kv=miss
- Model host span: condensed-anchor {model_variant, batch_size, seq_len, kv_status, model_start_ms, model_end_ms} (emit as JSON string in span tag)

If this direction looks sensible I will convert this draft into a short PRD and a small spike plan with concrete testcases (stitch-rate target, sample size, and dashboard wireframes).

End of proposal (working notes).

Changelog: 2024-11-07 initial draft by Priya; 2024-11-12 added sampling heuristics (Marcus); 2025-01-15 revised UX and milestone dates (Liam)
